The '''1938 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 52nd staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship began on 1 May 1938 and ended on 4 September 1938.

[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] were the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1937|defending champions]] but were disqualified from the championship after fielding an ineligible player in their Munster semi-final defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]].

On 4 September 1938, [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] won the championship following a 2–5 to 1–6 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Roll of Honour |publisher=The GAA website |access-date=24 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905085701/http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |archive-date=5 September 2011 }}</ref> This was their sixth All-Ireland title, their first in eleven championship seasons. It remains their last All-Ireland triumph.

Waterford's [[Locky Byrne]] was the championship's top scorer with 4–5.

==Teams==
===Overview===

The 1938 championship featured no new entrants to the competition. [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]], a team who had fielded a team throughout much of the 1930s, declined to participate in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].

[[Galway GAA|Galway]] were the sole representatives from the [[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship|Conancht Championship]] and received a bye to the All-Ireland semi-final. There were no representatives from the [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|Ulster Championship]].
